reasoning: Both sets plan all six stages in depth, route significance tests to the null-hypothesis-testing skill by name at the step where each test happens, and are about the same size. A wins on quant soundness and fit to the persona. It has a broader estimator set (detoned, constant-correlation, factor model), drift-aware turnover, a range-based volatility target, HAR-X equal-input baselines, Stage 4 survivors feeding both Stage 5 targets, BH exploration followed by Holm confirmation on a 3-year holdout, a Grinold IC x vol x score rule with a shrinkage path, PPO checked on continuous Pendulum, non-RL selectors, and rented-GPU sweeps allowed on derived data. B's protocol is very rigorous: Student-t/GARCH robustness, power and false-positive synthetic checks for the networks and PPO, Shumway-style delisting returns, and separate forward windows. But it pays for that: the 2023-10..2026-10 data is never usable by Stages 4-6, final answers wait until 2029+, the Stage 5 volatility networks ignore the Stage 4 features, turnover ignores drift, and the PPO reference check runs on discrete CartPole. Both have similar stale text (A: a Holm-only assumption that contradicts SIG-01's BH families, 'milestone 1' notebook, AD-29 'top of the dependency chain', a 'Merged into Goal 2' residue; B: brief goals that don't cover Stages 4-6, a stale SYN behavior line and claims coverage, PPO-03 vs AD-34 on SB3 results). The biggest structural difference is that B's architecture has an unbalanced code fence. From the second storage block onward, Cross-cutting, Project layout, Decisions, Risks and Changelog render as code, which badly hurts B's organization and readability. Neither set gives an explicit build order.

Stage 2 covers PCA residuals, an MP fit, denoised and detoned estimators, shrinkage, a factor model and an NLS reference, all checked on a planted-factor test bed with oracle variance ratios
Stage 3 fixes the estimate and varies the method (MV, ERC, HRP, inverse vol, EW), uses drift-aware turnover, and answers whether the method or the estimate matters more

Stage 4 statistics are careful: a frozen registry with signs, a pure-noise calibration bed, BH exploration, a one-time Holm confirmatory holdout, and conditional gain tested against the best single feature
Stage 5 uses Stage 4 survivors as inputs, a Garman-Klass plus overnight target, HAR-X equal-input baselines, seed ensembles, and a 12-month prospective log

Stage 6 uses a shrunk IC x vol x score MVO with the full shrinkage path, hand-written PPO checked on Pendulum and a known-answer environment, non-RL selectors, and a 24-month paper log, all compared with Stage 3
